pr.title: Tell every Projector repository to open pull requests as drafts
pr.head: 60716d3c04de8b1f0ce40044b1fca1f7f9815027

summary: Every repository that adopts Projector carries a section of agent instructions in its AGENTS.md, between <!-- projector:begin N --> and <!-- projector:end --> markers. project init writes that section from the template src/projector/templates/agents-block.md, and project check warns when a repository's copy is older than the template the CLI ships. Every agent session in the repository reads it, whichever skill the session runs.

Projector's review loop uses a pull request's draft state as its sign-off: a draft means no clean review has read the head yet, and project review publish marks the pull request ready when one does. That works only if pull requests start as drafts. Before this change, the rule to open them that way lived only in the implement skill and in this repository's own hand-written instructions, so an agent in another repository that opened a pull request without implement opened it ready, and it looked signed off before any review.

This change adds the rule to the template as version 4: open every pull request as a draft, each layer of a stack included, and never mark your own draft ready, because a clean review clears it. Adopting repositories get it after a release, when project check reports their section as outdated and project init refreshes it.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Section or block: the generated part of AGENTS.md between the Projector markers.
  • Template version: the integer in the template's begin marker, which check compares with a repository's copy.
  • Pinned hash: the SHA-256 of each template version, recorded in a test so the text cannot change without a version bump.

groups.title: The generated instructions gain a draft rule
groups.kicker: Template version 4 and this repository's re-rendered copy
intro: The template is the text project init writes into every adopting repository's AGENTS.md. Its version lives in its own begin marker, so bumping the marker from 3 to 4 is the whole version change: src/projector/instructions.py reads the version from the template rather than from a constant.

The new paragraph sits after the GitHub writing rules and before the stack rules. Its wording follows the implement skill, which already tells agents to open single pull requests and every stack layer as drafts, and the fix-pr skill, which tells them never to undraft by hand. This repository's own AGENTS.md (which CLAUDE.md links to) is re-rendered from the template so its copy stays current.

checks.text: The block in AGENTS.md matches the template with {projects_dir} rendered as docs/projects: project check at the head reports neither instructions-edited nor instructions-outdated.

files.note: The template every adopting repository's section is rendered from. It bumps to version 4 and adds the draft paragraph.

checks.text: The exception in the last sentence, that a clean review clears a draft, is what project review publish does when it marks a clean self-reviewed pull request ready. A fix-pr hold only ever turns a pull request draft, so it does not conflict with this rule.

Upgrading from version 3 works: in a throwaway Git repository with a version 3 block below hand-written lines, check warned about version 3, init --no-site --no-publish-rule printed updated AGENTS.md, a second check was clean, and the hand-written lines stayed at the top.

files.note: This repository's own instructions, with the generated section re-rendered at version 4.

checks.text: The hand-written "Hand work over for review" section above the markers already states this rule, with an extra warning about undrafting once a red test passes. The two copies now say the same thing.

groups.title: The pinned hash and the CLI reference follow
groups.kicker: A new pinned hash and two documentation updates
intro: A test pins the SHA-256 of each template version, so changing the template's text without bumping its version fails the suite. This change adds the hash for version 4. The CLI reference, docs/cli.md, lists what the generated section covers and shows a sample check warning; both now describe version 4.

checks.text: The full gate passes at the head: 801 tests OK (skipped=1), project check clean, both claude plugin validate runs passed, and git diff --check printed nothing.

files.note: Lists the draft rule among the section's contents and updates the sample outdated-section warning to version 3 → 4.
